extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (ECRs), prospective review mentors, and journal editors interested in peer-review mentoring and open peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Description and requirements for PREreview's mentoring programs (cohort-based and self-guided) that train ECRs to write constructive open peer reviews, pair them with mentors, and produce review outputs discoverable by journal editors. Includes live-streamed preprint journal-club guidance and diversity/accessibility goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train ECRs on how to write constructive manuscript reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Train ECRs on how to write constructive manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program curriculum explicitly focuses on 'strategies to write constructive reviews'; cohort-based participants publish reviews on PREreview.org as practice and to build open peer review profiles. Mentors provide constructive feedback on mentees' manuscript reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and combat biases; understand systems of oppression in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Train ECRs on how to recognize and combat biases, and understand systems of oppression as they manifest within the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum includes elements of implicit bias and how systems of oppression manifest in science; program aims to help mentees 'recognize and challenge their own internal biases that may influence their ability to remain objective when reviewing.' Stage 3 and 4 training includes deeper work on these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pair ECRs with experienced reviewers and journal editors for mentorship and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Pair ECRs with more experienced reviewers and journal editors who provide mentorship and constructive feedback to writing manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship modalities include one-to-one RT/RM calls, monthly ART/AR calls, mentor-provided feedback on draft reviews, and mentor training (e.g., Mentor Thought Exercise video) to encourage supportive, nurturing, safe mentoring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help ECRs access a support network of peers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Help ECRs access a support network of peers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program provides community calls, peer-to-peer support chats, and opportunities to meet journal editors and topic experts through events (e.g., live-streamed preprint journal clubs) to build networks and professional connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase racial diversity in the peer reviewer pool (50% pilot reservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help bring more racial diversity to the peer reviewer pool—in the pilot we reserved 50% of the mentee slots to applicants who self-identified as underrepresented racial minorities as defined by the National Science Foundation (NSF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pilot used NSF's U.S.-based definition (includes Black/African Americans, LatinX, Indigenous/First Peoples/American Indians & Alaskan Natives); organizers acknowledge limitations (time zones, staff, U.S.-centric definition) and intend to expand to be more globally inclusive as resources allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a database / Trained Reviewer list accessible to journal editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Work together with mentors to build a database of trained reviewers that journal editors can easily access when selecting reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of program stages and publication of a set number of highly scored manuscript reviews on PREreview.org are used to add participants to a 'Trained Reviewer' list for editorial prospecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages of Engagement defined by prior peer-review experience
rubrics_metrics.description: We define four 'Stages of Engagement' (Stage 1 Review Trainees, Stage 2 Advanced Review Trainees, Stage 3 Advanced Reviewer, Stage 4 Review Mentors) that participants enter based on their experience with writing manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage definitions: Stage 1 = little-to-no experience; Stage 2 = completed 2–5 manuscript reviews in traditional or open settings; Stage 3 = completed at least 6 manuscript reviews; Stage 4 = experienced reviewers or journal editors or those who completed stage 3. Each stage has different expected activities and eligibility to mentor/be added to Trained Reviewer list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion/output requirements: publish specified numbers of preprint reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage completion is tied to publishing reviews on PREreview.org: RTs (stage 1) publish 2 preprint reviews; ARTs (stage 2) publish an additional 4 preprint reviews (total 6) to build profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With a total of 6 highly scored manuscript reviews, ARTs are added to the Trained Reviewer list for editorial prospecting and qualify to join stage 3. Stage 1 completion readies participants to join stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort-based component structure and engagement expectations (14 weeks)
rubrics_metrics.description: 14-week cohort-based component where RTs engage in community calls, peer-to-peer support chats, and one-to-one RTs/RMs calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum focuses on 'critical evaluation of emerging scientific literature,' 'strategies to write constructive reviews,' 'understanding how systems of oppression manifest within the scientific enterprise,' and 'helping mentees recognize and challenge their own internal biases.' Provides peer-to-peer support and mentorship/leadership training for future mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-guided component structure and expected interactions (8 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: 8-month self-guided component where ARTs have access to recorded training materials and are paired with ARs for monthly meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARTs consume recorded videos and documents at their own pace, meet ARs for 30–60 minute calls once a month, and—supported by mentors—complete and publish 4 preprint reviews on PREreview.org. ARs are asked to watch the Mentor Thought Exercise video prior to first call to foster supportive mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-streamed preprint journal clubs: guided, inclusive discussion format
rubrics_metrics.description: Live-streamed preprint journal clubs are topic-centered, interactive events live-streamed via video-conference that follow guided discussion questions to encourage diverse methods of participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles include two facilitators, optional topic experts, optional preprint authors, and researchers worldwide. The format aims to support underrepresented voices and early-career researchers and to collaboratively improve preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event outputs: create peer review reports from journal clubs that can integrate into journal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: After the call, the team summarizes the discussion into a peer review report that is openly shared on PREreview and can be integrated into journal-organized peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given where a PREreview report was included as reviewer #3 in eLife's peer review of a bioRxiv preprint. Reports serve both public feedback and potential formal journal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor conduct and training expectations (supportive, nurturing, safe space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors are expected to develop a supportive, nurturing, and safe space for mentees and to volunteer time to train RTs (stage 4 RMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor preparation includes watching the 'Mentor Thought Exercise' video and engaging in mentor/leadership training during the cohort to ensure constructive feedback and inclusive mentoring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and pilot implementation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot selection process, timeline, and capacity constraints influenced participant selection and geographic reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot launched Oct 2020; applications for stages 1–3 were open for 2 weeks; selected numbers were limited (10 stage 1, 8 stage 2 and 3, 9 stage 4). Time zone and staff constraints led to primarily U.S. and European accommodation; organizers commit to re-evaluating and expanding inclusivity as resources allow.
